title: Forged writs of habeas corpus for black kids in jail
summary: He tells how he freed Black kids from Dallas jails with writs signed by a judge.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: One of the things I used to do...in Dallas they had a thing called...they had two jails, the city jail and the county jail. If you were in the city jail, arrested for something, and they transferred you to the county jail, after they filed charges against you...well, they had a thing called a writ of habeas corpus. The lawyer would get this and the judge would

sign it. But I don't exactly remember how I...whether I used to swipe them from the lawyer...but anyway, I'd get the kid's name, you understand, and then I'd put it on that thing and then take it to a judge...this one judge who knew when I first used to take them for a lawyer . Then I'd take them to this judge and he'd always sign it. And I got a lot of black kids out of jail that way. And they never did catch on to it. I guess if they'd caught on to it I'd have really went to Gatesville. I was about 15. That was just one of the many things I used to do extracurricular. (Laughter).
